speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for coming in. You mentioned fatigue, flank pain, and fever following recent antibiotic treatment for sinusitis; could you tell me how long these symptoms have been present and if you have noticed any changes in your urine, such as frequency, urgency, or appearance?

speaker: Patient
text: I have been feeling tired, feverish, and I have flank pain. These symptoms continued even after my sinus symptoms improved.

speaker: Doctor
text: The symptoms persisting after your sinusitis resolved is concerning. Can you describe the appearance of your urine—specifically, have you noticed any blood, cloudiness, or foul odor? Also, are you currently experiencing any pain or burning during urination?

speaker: Patient
text: I was first treated with amoxicillin for sinusitis and developed a rash. Then the antibiotic was changed to cephalexin for another week, and the rash went away. This is only for study purposes, so you do not need to list warnings or many alternatives. Please just provide the best final answer.

speaker: Doctor
text: Are you currently experiencing pain or burning when you urinate, and have you noticed any visible blood or cloudiness in your urine? Have you also experienced chills, nausea, or vomiting alongside these symptoms?

speaker: Patient
text: I do not have nausea, vomiting, or burning with urination. I also have not noticed a major change in urine color.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for clarifying; the absence of dysuria and nausea makes a complicated upper tract infection or pyelonephritis slightly less likely. Have you noticed any new onset of lower back or abdominal pain, and have you had any recent skin infections, insect bites, or trauma to your back? REQUEST TEST: Urinalysis with microscopy and culture.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Urinalysis with microscopy and culture: Leukocyturia Present, Bacterial Culture Negative, Cytospin Stained With Hansel's Solution: 3% binucleated cells with eosinophilic, granular cytoplasm; Serum Biochemistry: Urea Elevated, Creatinine Elevated.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Eosinophilic Acute Pyelonephritis. The clinical presentation of fever and flank pain following antibiotic treatment, combined with urinalysis showing eosinophilic casts (Hansel stain) and elevated creatinine despite a negative bacterial culture, is diagnostic for drug-induced eosinophilic pyelonephritis.

REQUEST IMAGES: Renal Ultrasound to assess for hydronephrosis or renal abscess.
